metadata.title: Boundary behavior for a singular quasi-linear elliptic equation

nodes.name: Singular quasi-linear elliptic problem (P)
nodes.statement: The singular quasi-linear problem: -div(a(u)Du) + a'(u)/2 |Du|^2 = f(u) in Omega, u > 0 in Omega, u = 0 on the boundary of Omega, where Omega is a smooth bounded domain in R^N.

nodes.name: Assumption on the diffusion coefficient a
nodes.statement: The function a:(0,+infty)->(0,+infty) is C^1, bounded away from zero, and satisfies lim_{s->0+} a(s) s^{2mu} = a_0 for some 0 <= mu < 1 and a_0 > 0.

nodes.name: Assumption on the source term f
nodes.statement: The function f:(0,+infty)->(0,+infty) is C^1 and satisfies lim_{s->0+} f(s) s^gamma = f_0 for some gamma > 1 and f_0 > 0.

nodes.name: Coupling condition between a and f
nodes.statement: The functions a and f satisfy the monotonicity coupling condition 2f'(s)a(s) <= f(s)a'(s) for every s > 0.

nodes.name: Main theorem: existence, uniqueness, and boundary behavior
nodes.statement: Problem (P) has a unique solution u in C^2(Omega) cap C(bar Omega) with sharp two-sided boundary estimates for u and an upper bound for |Du| in terms of d(x, partial Omega), along with regularity conclusions depending on the relationship between gamma and mu.
assumptions: Omega is a smooth bounded domain in R^N
a:(0,+infty)->(0,+infty) is C^1, bounded away from zero, with lim_{s->0+} a(s)s^{2mu} = a_0 > 0 for some 0 <= mu < 1
f:(0,+infty)->(0,+infty) is C^1 with lim_{s->0+} f(s)s^gamma = f_0 > 0 for some gamma > 1
conclusions: There exists a unique solution u in C^2(Omega) cap C(bar Omega)
There exist Gamma, Gamma', Gamma'' > 0 such that Gamma d(x,partial Omega)^{2/(1+gamma-2mu)} <= u(x) <= Gamma' d(x,partial Omega)^{2/(1+gamma-2mu)} as d(x,partial Omega) -> 0
|Du(x)| <= Gamma'' d(x,partial Omega)^{(1-gamma+2mu)/(1+gamma-2mu)} as d(x,partial Omega) -> 0
u is Lipschitz on bar Omega if 1 < gamma <= 1+2mu
u is Holder continuous with exponent 2/(1+gamma-2mu) on bar Omega if gamma > 1+2mu
u belongs to H^1_0(Omega) if gamma < 3-2mu

nodes.name: Change of variable function g via Cauchy problem
nodes.statement: The function g in C^2((0,+infty)) cap C([0,+infty)) is defined as the unique solution to g'(s) = 1/sqrt(a(g(s))) for s > 0, g(0) = 0, g(s) > 0 for s > 0. Equivalently, integral from 0 to g(s) of sqrt(a(xi)) dxi = s.

nodes.name: Reduction to semilinear problem via change of variable
nodes.statement: Setting v = g^{-1}(u) and h(s) := f(g(s))/sqrt(a(g(s))), the quasi-linear problem (P) for u is equivalent to the semilinear problem -Delta v = h(v) in Omega, v > 0 in Omega, v = 0 on partial Omega.

nodes.name: Asymptotic behavior of g at zero
nodes.statement: For 0 <= mu < 1, lim_{s->0+} g(s)/s^{1/(1-mu)} = (1-mu)^{1/(1-mu)} a_0^{1/(2(mu-1))}. This is proved by l'Hopital's rule using the Cauchy problem for g and the assumption on a.

nodes.name: Asymptotic behavior of h at zero
nodes.statement: lim_{s->0+} h(s)/s^{(mu-gamma)/(1-mu)} = f_0 a_0^{(1-gamma)/(2(mu-1))} (1-mu)^{-(gamma-mu)/(1-mu)}. This follows from the asymptotics of a, f, and g at zero.

nodes.name: Three key properties of h = f(g(.))/sqrt(a(g(.)))
nodes.statement: The function h(s) = f(g(s))/sqrt(a(g(s))) satisfies: (1) integrability at infinity, (2) h(s) -> +infty as s -> 0+, and (3) s -> h(s) is nonincreasing on (0,+infty).
assumptions: a(s) ~ a_infty s^k as s -> +infty for some k >= 0, a_infty > 0
f(s) ~ f_infty s^{-p} as s -> +infty for some p > 1, f_infty > 0
conclusions: integral from 1 to +infty of f(g(s))/sqrt(a(g(s))) ds < +infty
The map s -> f(g(s))/sqrt(a(g(s))) is nonincreasing

nodes.name: Asymptotic behavior of integral of f from g(s) to infinity
nodes.statement: For gamma > 1 and 0 <= mu < 1: lim_{s->0+} (integral from g(s) to +infty of f(xi) dxi) / s^{(1-gamma)/(1-mu)} = f_0 a_0^{(gamma-1)/(2(1-mu))} (gamma-1)^{-1} (1-mu)^{-(gamma-1)/(1-mu)}. Proved by l'Hopital's rule using the asymptotics of g.

nodes.name: Auxiliary ODE problem for phi
nodes.statement: For l >= 0, the function phi in C([0,+infty)) cap C^2((0,+infty)) is the unique solution of phi'(s) = sqrt(l^2 + 2 integral from g(phi(s)) to +infty of f(xi) dxi) for s > 0, phi(0) = 0, phi(s) > 0 for s > 0, with phi'(s) -> l and phi(s) -> +infty as s -> +infty.

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness of phi
nodes.statement: For every l >= 0, there exists a unique solution phi to the auxiliary ODE problem. This follows from applying Lemma 1.3 of [zhangcheng] using the properties of h.
assumptions: The three properties of h (integrability, blow-up at zero, monotonicity)
conclusions: There exists a unique phi in C([0,+infty)) cap C^2((0,+infty)) solving the auxiliary ODE problem

nodes.name: Asymptotic behavior of phi at zero
nodes.statement: For gamma > 1, 0 <= mu < 1, and l >= 0: lim_{s->0+} phi(s)/s^{(2-2mu)/(1+gamma-2mu)} = C(gamma,mu,a_0,f_0), where C is an explicit positive constant involving gamma, mu, a_0, f_0. Proved by l'Hopital's rule and the asymptotics of the integral of f.

nodes.name: Proof of the main theorem
nodes.statement: The proof proceeds by: (1) reducing the quasi-linear problem to a semilinear one -Delta v = h(v) via the change of variable g; (2) establishing the asymptotics of g, h, and the auxiliary function phi at zero; (3) applying the existence/uniqueness result of Crandall-Rabinowitz-Tartar for the semilinear problem; (4) transferring the boundary estimates for v back to u using the asymptotics of g; (5) deriving gradient estimates and regularity (Lipschitz, Holder, Sobolev) from the boundary behavior.

nodes.name: Remark on Lipschitz continuity range
nodes.statement: If gamma < 1, combining the asymptotics of h with Theorem 2.25 of [craRabTar], any solution v of -Delta v = h(v) is Lipschitz continuous, and so is u = g(v) since g is Lipschitz on (0,+infty). This extends the Lipschitz range beyond that stated in the main theorem.
assumptions: a is bounded away from zero
conclusions: The solution u is Lipschitz continuous up to the boundary

nodes.name: Remark on global estimates on all of bar Omega
nodes.statement: Using Theorem 1.3 of [zhangcheng] in place of Theorems 2.2 and 2.5 of [craRabTar], one can obtain global estimates for u and |Du| valid on the whole bar Omega (not just near the boundary), expressed in terms of g and phi composed with d(x, partial Omega).
conclusions: Global two-sided bounds: g(Lambda_1 phi(d(x,partial Omega))) <= u(x) <= g(Lambda_2 phi(d(x,partial Omega))) for x in bar Omega
Global gradient bound: |Du(x)| <= Lambda_3 [d h(Lambda_4 phi(d)) + phi(d)/d] / sqrt(a(u(x))) for x in bar Omega

nodes.name: Remark on convexity of superlevel sets
nodes.statement: Defining psi(s) = integral from 0 to s of 1/sqrt(2 H(xi)) dxi where H(s) = integral from s to +infty of h(xi) dxi, and setting w = -psi(v), one obtains Delta w = f(w,Dw) with w = 0 on partial Omega. When f > 0 and z -> 1/f(z,.) is convex, convexity of Omega implies convexity of w, which in turn gives convexity of superlevel sets of u.
assumptions: v is a smooth positive solution of -Delta v = h(v)
conclusions: The function w = -psi(v) may be convex
Superlevel sets of u may be convex since u = g(psi^{-1}(-w)) with g o psi^{-1} strictly increasing
